systemOverview.name: Enhanced Validation System
systemOverview.purpose: Agent-driven validation system with automatic extension capabilities, safety framework, and comprehensive monitoring

backend.description: Backend/Service Tasks - Service discovery, command routing, backend integration

expectedBehavior.serviceTesting: Starts minimal-backend service and tests health checks
expectedBehavior.commandExecution: Tests command routing with success=true validation
expectedBehavior.contentValidation: Validates service configuration files contain endpoint data

ui.description: UI/Interface Tasks - Menu structure, CLI interface consistency, VSCode integration, UX validation

expectedBehavior.menuValidation: Checks menu structure and navigation patterns
expectedBehavior.cliConsistency: Validates CLI interface consistency and error handling
expectedBehavior.vscodeIntegration: Verifies .vscode configuration files are valid JSON
expectedBehavior.uxFlow: Tests user experience patterns and state management

core.description: Core System Tasks - Configuration integrity, state management, resource handling, type system consistency

expectedBehavior.configIntegrity: Validates JSON/TS configuration files parse correctly
expectedBehavior.stateManagement: Checks state management patterns and error handling

build.description: Compilation/Build Tasks - TypeScript fixes, library compatibility, build configuration

expectedBehavior.artifactVerification: Verifies build artifacts exist in dist/build/out directories

quality.description: Code Quality Tasks - ESLint compliance, code complexity analysis, technical debt assessment, refactoring recommendations

expectedBehavior.complexityAnalysis: Calculates cyclomatic complexity for code files
expectedBehavior.debtAssessment: Scans for TODO/FIXME/HACK patterns and technical debt indicators
expectedBehavior.refactoringRecommendations: Identifies long functions, duplicate code, deep nesting
expectedBehavior.maintainabilityScoring: Provides 0-100 maintainability score based on multiple factors

architecture.description: Architectural validation - Pattern changes, system design

feature.description: Feature enhancement validation - New capabilities, optimizations

subagent.description: Subagent workflow validation - Agent handoff workflows

backend.testStrategy: Start services, execute health checks, validate service registration files
errorDiagnostics: Service startup failures - check examples/minimal-backend directory
Health check failures - verify curl command and port 3004 availability
Registration failures - check .templum/services directory exists and has JSON files
Timeout errors - increase timeout for large projects or exclude large directories

ui.testStrategy: Analyze interface files for patterns, validate VSCode config, check accessibility
errorDiagnostics: No menu files found - expected behavior if project has no UI components
VSCode config errors - check .vscode/*.json files for valid JSON syntax
UX flow issues - look for state management and error handling patterns

core.testStrategy: Validate configurations, check TypeScript compilation, verify service patterns
errorDiagnostics: Config validation errors - check JSON syntax in configuration files
TypeScript compilation failures - review compiler output for specific errors
Service pattern issues - look for proper class/interface definitions

build.testStrategy: Execute build commands, check TypeScript compilation, verify dependencies
errorDiagnostics: Build command missing - add build script to package.json or update valconfig.json
TypeScript errors - resolve compilation issues before proceeding
Dependency conflicts - resolve npm dependency issues
No build artifacts - may be normal for projects without build output

quality.directoryScoping: Uses provided scope patterns or defaults to **/*.ts, **/*.js
quality.testStrategy: Analyze code complexity, scan for technical debt, generate refactoring recommendations
errorDiagnostics: High complexity - consider breaking large functions into smaller ones
Technical debt - address TODO/FIXME comments and simplify code patterns
Low maintainability - improve commenting, reduce nesting, simplify functions

scopeTesting.strategy: Test each validator with different scope patterns to verify correct file discovery and pattern matching

testCases.name: Default scope validation
testCases.expectedBehavior: Should use validator's default scope patterns

testCases.name: Custom scope validation
testCases.expectedBehavior: Should limit validation to TypeScript files in src directory

testCases.name: Multi-pattern scope validation
testCases.expectedBehavior: Should validate TypeScript in src and JavaScript in test directories

testCases.name: Empty scope validation
testCases.expectedBehavior: Should handle gracefully with appropriate warnings or skips

errorRecovery.strategy: Test system behavior under various error conditions

testCases.name: Invalid project configuration
testCases.expectedBehavior: Should provide clear error message and configuration guidance

testCases.name: Missing dependencies
testCases.setup: Test on system without Node.js or required tools
testCases.expectedBehavior: Should identify missing dependencies and provide installation guidance

testCases.name: Timeout conditions
testCases.setup: Use very short timeout or very large project
testCases.expectedBehavior: Should timeout gracefully and provide meaningful error messages

testCases.name: Permission errors
testCases.setup: Test with read-only file system or restricted permissions
testCases.expectedBehavior: Should handle permission errors without crashing

behaviorVerification.strategy: Verify each validator does what it claims to do
behaviorVerification.approach: Create controlled test environments with known conditions and verify expected outcomes
validationPoints: Backend validator actually starts services and tests connectivity
Build validator executes actual build commands and checks artifacts
UI validator finds and analyzes interface files correctly
Core validator performs real TypeScript compilation checks
Quality validator calculates meaningful complexity and debt metrics

steps: 1. Check project configuration exists and is valid JSON
2. Verify project directory path is correct and accessible
3. Confirm report directory exists (create manually if needed)
4. Test with simple scope first, then expand
5. Check system dependencies (Node.js, npm, TypeScript, etc.)

projectNotFound.symptom: Project configuration missing or invalid path
projectNotFound.solution: Verify project name matches config file, check project_directory path

reportDirectoryError.solution: Create the directory specified in valconfig.json report_location

timeoutErrors.solution: Increase timeout in valconfig.json or optimize scope patterns

dependencyMissing.symptom: Command not found or execution errors
dependencyMissing.solution: Install required dependencies (npm, TypeScript, ESLint, etc.)

recommendations: Start with health-check command to verify system status
Test each category individually before comprehensive validation
Use scoped validation for large projects to improve performance
Monitor timeouts and adjust configuration as needed
Verify all required directories exist before running validation
Keep validation task-ids descriptive for better tracking and debugging
Review validator self-diagnostics output for capability verification
executionHints: Validation Agents should test incrementally: health check → individual validators → scoped validation → full validation
Pay attention to status codes: 0 = success, 1 = validation failed, other = system error
Verification approach: Compare expected behaviors with actual validator outputs
Error analysis: Use evidence arrays and error messages to identify root causes
Performance monitoring: Track validation duration and timeout patterns
Report validation: Ensure generated reports contain expected evidence and recommendations

metadata.contextTokensUsed: Extensive analysis of validation system architecture and implementations
